title: Lusin's theorem with compact sets for Borel maps ℝ^P → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N) and an arbitrary measure on a finite-measure Borel set
statement: Let P, N ∈ ℕ, μ a measure on the Borel sets of ℝ^P, and u : ℝ^P → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N) Borel. Let A ⊆ ℝ^P be Borel with μ(A) < ∞ and let ε ∈ (0, ∞]. Then there is a compact set C ⊆ A with μ(A ∖ C) < ε such that u is continuous on C.
lean_statement: ∀ (P N : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Eucl P)) (u : Eucl P → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N)), Measurable u → ∀ A : Set (Eucl P), MeasurableSet A → μ A ≠ ∞ → ∀ ε : ℝ≥0∞, ε ≠ 0 → ∃ C : Set (Eucl P), IsCompact C ∧ C ⊆ A ∧ μ (A \ C) < ε ∧ ContinuousOn u C
